Question.Question: If a message fails all retries, why is its offset still committed?
Question.GroundTruth: Because the message has already been written to the DLQ, so it is not lost. Committing prevents the consumer from re-reading the same poison message forever and blocking the partition. The trade-off is that if the DLQ write itself fails, the error is only logged and the offset is still committed, so that message is dropped. Overall semantics are at-least-once.
